theme: 3 terms on property wrappers: the type that adds logic to a property, the value it holds, and the extra value behind the dollar sign

terms.definition: A type marked with `@propertyWrapper` that adds the same extra logic to every property it is attached to.
terms.example: Let's write a Property Wrapper so every name is stored in capitals.

terms.definition: The value inside a Property Wrapper that you read and write through the property's normal name.
terms.example: When you read `count`, you get the Wrapped Value, not the wrapper.

terms.definition: An extra value a Property Wrapper can expose, which you reach with a dollar sign before the property name.
terms.example: `$score` is the Projected Value, so it's not the score itself.

video.description:
Learn to explain property wrappers in Swift: Property Wrapper, Wrapped Value & Projected Value, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Property Wrapper - A type marked with `@propertyWrapper` that adds the same extra logic to every property it is attached to.
Wrapped Value - The value inside a Property Wrapper that you read and write through the property's normal name.
Projected Value - An extra value a Property Wrapper can expose, which you reach with a dollar sign before the property name.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain property wrappers in English?

dialogue.title: What does @Clamped do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a Property Wrapper. It runs extra code every time `volume` is set.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So when I set `volume` to 150, it becomes 100?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The Wrapped Value goes through `min`, so it stops at 100.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wait, so `volume` is really the Wrapped Value?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Reading `volume` reads the Wrapped Value inside `Clamped`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then what is `$volume`? I saw it in the slider code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the Projected Value. Here it's a `Bool` that says `volume` is at the max.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh, I thought the dollar sign always meant a binding.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In SwiftUI it often does, but each Property Wrapper picks its own Projected Value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Property Wrapper for shared logic, Wrapped Value for the data, Projected Value for extras.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every setter repeats the same check.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Move it into a Property Wrapper.
